The builder's pack already supplies the full 8-angle orbit and a 30-frame motion sheet on HARDWARE at a source state byte-identical to HEAD for both edited files, so the finding does not rest on my capture — mine exists only to show the defect survives the V2 compositor and SSAO that landed after the pinned sha. Stated rather than rounded up to 8.

I DID NOT RE-RENT A POD. Every hardware frame I reason from is the builder's, re-read rather than re-run. Justified because both edited files are byte-identical between the pinned sha 03ba530d47 and HEAD and the working tree is clean for both — but it is a reuse of someone else's arms, not an independent hardware replication, and a later critic should know that.

RI-VIS08 sections B2 (triangle budget), B4 (texel density), B5 (contact-shadow grounding), B6 (subsurface response) and ALL of section C (the animation measurables) were not computed. They are measured on surfaces that are not rasterised; a texel density for a mesh that produces no fragment is a number about nothing. Recorded as `not_run` with the reason rather than scored as fail.

I DID NOT MEASURE THE TWO RESIDUAL RISKS the builder named and left unmeasured — shader program count after the copy seam multiplies compiles, and the unbounded `shadedMaterials` Set. Both are in `secondary_observations`; neither is the biggest gap and neither is closed.

MY OWN `NO-SHADER-ERROR-ON-THE-CONSOLE` CHECK PASSES AND PROVES NOTHING. The console listener attaches after `launchForCapture` has already booted the page, so a boot-time compile error is missed. It is retained as a weak second witness and labelled as such inside the tool. The authoritative reading is `program.diagnostics.runnable`, read out of the renderer itself.

I DID NOT VERIFY WHETHER ANY OTHER PIECE'S CHANGE ALSO FAILS TO LINK. My probe scans actor bodies and actor equipment only. A whole-scene sweep for `runnable === false` is the durable tripwire I am asking for in the remedy, and I did not build it into the standing census myself — rule 23, that is the next builder's edit and I am not grading my own repair.
headline: FAIL, 1/10. The F1 fix stops the player's body and every NPC's body from being drawn, and it is live at HEAD. Two shader identifiers collide — `uniform float uWetness` and `float esWet` are each declared by both installSurfaceShader and installWaterline once the fix makes them chain — and 66 of 124 actor-body programs report runnable:false with 'redefinition'. Three of the brief's four attacks failed: the pinned baseline, the revert and the ground control are all sound.

the_finding.what: installWaterline used to ASSIGN onBeforeCompile, which deleted installSurfaceShader's hook. This piece made it CHAIN (loss E in the builder's own table). Chaining puts both fragment preambles into one program, and they collide on two identifiers.
collisions: uniform float uWetness — visual-foundation.js:521 and actor.js:302
the_finding.driver_says: runnable:false, 'ERROR: 0:81: uWetness : redefinition', 'ERROR: 0:1724: esWet : redefinition' — read from the live renderer's program.diagnostics at HEAD, not inferred from source
the_finding.population: 124 actor-body materials across the player and every NPC/enemy, saxhleel and humanoid families. 66 of 124 had been compiled at the sampling instant; every one of those 66 failed to link. The other 58 are null, not green.
the_finding.blast_radius_is_bounded_and_that_is_the_: installWaterline is called at exactly one site, actor.js:607, inside the ['cloth','skin'] body loop. So only actor BODIES break. 65 of 65 equipment and frill control materials carry 0 duplicates and 0 link failures — and that is exactly what the frames show: the horns, eyes, frills, equipment, shield and weapon still draw while the head, arms, legs and torso do not.
the_finding.live_at_head: game/src/render/visual-foundation.js and game/src/render/actor.js are byte-identical between 03ba530d47 and HEAD fb42ad10, working tree clean for both.

what_i_tried_to_break_and_could_not: THE PINNED BASELINE IS REAL. 03ba530d47's two files md5 to 5084d503… and a3a0a740…, byte-identical to the pre-md5 in the Pod's own revert.log, and run.json records source.dirty false. The archive came from the sha, not from HEAD. HAZARDS §12 is genuinely handled.

THE REVERT WAS NOT SILENTLY INERT (run 1's failure mode). I reran `w1-30-copy-seam-patch.mjs --revert` myself on an isolated copy of the pinned sha and reproduced both post-md5 values exactly — then diffed those bytes IDENTICAL against 9ddeb512^, the true parent of the commit that introduced the fix. The two arms differ by the fix and by nothing else. This is a cleaner arm-freeze than anything else I have seen in this corpus.

THE GROUND CONTROL IS LIVE, NOT INERT. It moves 73.28% of pixels in the BEFORE arm against a 0.00% restore floor, with maxDelta identical to two decimals across arms and 37 of 37 selected materials carrying uniforms in both. An inert control is one that cannot move; this one moves in the arm where the defect is present, which is precisely what makes the player's 0.33% an absence rather than a broken harness.

THE CONSUMPTION PROBE CONSUMES THE SHIPPED PATH. It reads window.__ENGINE.renderer, traverses R.scene, selects from R.playerMesh and writes into the materials the shipped world built, never setting needsUpdate. Nothing is reimplemented. The RI-MTH07 shape is correct.

why_every_check_stayed_green: The census asks whether a hook installs uniforms, never whether the composed shader LINKS. `NO-HOOK-THREW` is the near miss: the hook does not throw, it emits illegal GLSL. The consumption probe measures a delta WITHIN an arm, and a material whose program does not link contributes zero to both the base and the perturbed frame, so it is invisible to a within-arm difference. mesh.visible stays true, pageErrors stays empty, and a link failure arrives on console.error which nothing was listening to. And delete-the-fix ran through the census alone — a frame comparison would have shown a body appearing.

answer_to_the_orchestrator.question: Is F1 good enough that re-running the blind Protocol A comparison is worth paying for now, or should F2 and F3 land first?
answer_to_the_orchestrator.answer: NEITHER. Do not pay for Protocol A, and do not wait for F2/F3 either. Close this gap first — it is a rename in one function and the gate for it already exists and is already red.
answer_to_the_orchestrator.why_not_protocol_a_now: Five blind judges would be shown a game whose characters are floating equipment with no bodies. They would not report on materials at all; they would report that. The comparison would burn its budget measuring a defect a two-line probe already names precisely, and the result would be uninterpretable as a materials verdict.
answer_to_the_orchestrator.why_not_f2_f3_first: F2 and F3 are contact shadows, AO and ambient fill — all of which land ON characters. Grounding and contact darkening judged against a character with no body is not a measurement. Landing them first means re-taking their evidence afterwards.
answer_to_the_orchestrator.the_order_i_recommend: 1) The rename in actor.js#installWaterline, gated on `node tools/visual/w1-f1-critic-shader-collision.mjs` going green — S, and the tool exists. 2) Move the runnable:false check into tools/visual/w1-30-surface-orphan-census.mjs so the standing census can see this class at all. 3) Re-take the two-arm frame evidence and re-run base-frame-ab.mjs, requiring the body PRESENT in both arms. 4) THEN F2/F3. 5) THEN Protocol A, once there is a body for the contact shadow to land on and a surface for the judges to judge.
answer_to_the_orchestrator.what_would_change_my_mind: If a hardware capture at HEAD showed the bodies present — i.e. if the software backend I captured on were somehow the cause. It is not: the builder's own RTX A5000 after-arm frames show the same absence at the same source state, and a GLSL redefinition is a parse error, not a driver behaviour. That is why I did not spend a Pod re-proving it.

i_did_not_repair_anything: Rule 23. I did not touch game/src. The remedy is a minimal executable specification in biggest_gap.remedy: preserve the copy seam (it is correct), rename two identifiers in one function, and add the missing tripwire. Named targets, named lines, named acceptance, named hard fail.
